clue.text: Tides swirling round end of bus stop

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the next piece
swirling waters churn about, so the letters of tides are stirred into a new order
end of picks the final letter of the word bus

explanation.surface: A busy coastal bus route halted by tides washing around the last stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' turns TIDES into DEIST, and 'round' puts S, from 'end of bus', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or leave off doing something, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Excitement about Switzerland's old silver coin

indicators.note: about means the first word surrounds the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: drama is excitement or commotion, as in 'there was a lot of drama'
CH is the international code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)

explanation.surface: A collector thrilled by an old Swiss silver coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The ''s' is a link; the coin is Greek, not Swiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was a silver coin of ancient Greece, and later the modern Greek currency before the euro.

clue.text: Cancel subscription to protect creditor

indicators.note: to protect means the first piece wraps itself around the abbreviation, shielding it

parts.note: sub is a short form of subscription, a membership fee
CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor

explanation.surface: Advice to cancel a subscription payment so that a lender is safeguarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is informal for calling it off or abandoning it.

clue.text: Streetwise leader's entreaty to graffiti artist?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of streetwise

parts.note: a prayer is an earnest request or plea

explanation.surface: A savvy street figure pleads with someone who tags walls.
explanation.definitionFit: A graffiti artist typically works with spray cans, so is one who sprays; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Try to get friend into new art and old Marian hymn music

parts.note: to have a ... something is to try it

indicators.note: to get one thing somewhere is to place it, here putting the friend in position
into means the friend is put inside the rearranged letters of art
new means the letters of art appear in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Instructions on combining a companion with modern art, alongside a medieval hymn to Mary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; the definition is the whole closing phrase, the hymn and its musical settings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stabat Mater is a thirteenth-century Latin hymn on the Virgin's sorrows at the cross, often set to music by composers.

clue.text: Upper-class chap snorting drugs to get things going

indicators.note: snorting means taking something in, so the chap holds the drugs inside

parts.note: a toff is British slang for a posh, upper-class man
E is slang for ecstasy, so two Es are drugs

explanation.surface: A posh man takes cocaine to liven up a party.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the first stroke from the tee starts the round, hence the idiom for beginning anything.

clue.text: Taliban to become an army unit

indicators.note: become signals the letters of the preceding words turning into something else

explanation.surface: Insurgents enlisting to form a regular military force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is part of the fodder, not a link: TALIBAN TO gives the nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A battalion is a large body of troops, part of a regiment or brigade.

clue.text: Pre-rest, naughty child moves unsteadily

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: naughty means misbehaving, so the letters of rest are unruly and rearranged

explanation.surface: Before a nap, a misbehaving toddler wobbles about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pre-' means the child comes before the shuffled letters; the hyphen glues it onto the word that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to walk shakily or sway as if about to fall.

clue.text: Vehicles, one after another, carrying assistance, turned up to support a major medical emergency

indicators.note: carrying means the pair of vehicles holds the next piece inside
one after another means the vehicle appears twice in succession

parts.note: a car is a vehicle; two of them make vehicles

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for assistance is read from bottom to top

parts.note: aid is help or assistance
a rest is something that supports, like an armrest

explanation.surface: A traffic pile-up of ambulances arriving at a serious medical crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; in a down entry 'turned up' reverses the help, which sits between the two vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: When the heart suddenly stops pumping, it is a life-threatening emergency needing immediate resuscitation.

clue.text: Couple stealing gold from home helper

indicators.note: stealing ... from means the gold is taken away from the helper

parts.note: an au pair is a young foreigner living with a family to help in the home
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A pair of thieves who pinch gold from a domestic helper.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of a kind together, the same as a couple.

clue.text: Money given to fourth in line, say, for property

parts.note: the real is the currency of Brazil
the press is called the fourth estate, coming after the three traditional estates of the realm

explanation.surface: Cash handed to an heir fourth in succession to buy land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fourth in line' suggests royal succession, but it is the fourth estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings, property in the legal sense.

clue.text: Round clubs for the old man

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
a woman's old man is her husband, informally hubby

explanation.surface: Golf clubs bought for a father as a round of gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Round and chubby both describe a plump, rounded figure.

clue.text: Let down by legal document about apartment

indicators.note: about means the document goes around the next word

parts.note: a deed is a signed legal document
a flat is the British word for an apartment

explanation.surface: Disappointed by the paperwork on a flat purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: Let down can mean both dispirited and having air released, and deflated covers each sense.

clue.text: Cruel and pointed remark by one born in late March?

parts.note: a barb is a cutting, pointed remark
Aries begins around 21 March, so someone born then is an Arian

explanation.surface: A sharp comment from an Aries person seems cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one born in late March?' is a star sign, not a date of birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, barbarian means savage, brutal and uncivilised.

clue.text: Damaged car banned in social event

indicators.note: damaged means the letters of the words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A wrecked car barred from a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn dance is a country gathering with folk dancing, a type of social occasion.

clue.text: Accommodation for archaeologists?

parts.note: lodgings are informally called ... in Britain, and excavation sites are an archaeologist's ...

explanation.surface: Where excavators lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is British slang for rented lodgings, and also the sites where archaeologists excavate.

clue.text: Part of the Koran found in ancient city in Saudi Arabia

indicators.note: in means the city is placed within the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: SA can stand for Saudi Arabia
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A passage of the Koran discovered at an ancient Saudi site.
explanation.definitionFit: A sura is one of the 114 chapters of the Koran.

clue.text: Set up celebrity with young man from the fifties

parts.note: a star is a celebrity
a Teddy boy, or Ted, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress

explanation.surface: A famous person framed alongside a 1950s youth.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up a business is to found or establish it, i.e. began it.

clue.text: One travelling out to north Germany

parts.note: passé means out of fashion

explanation.surface: A traveller heading off to northern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger is someone carried in a vehicle, a traveller who is not driving.

clue.text: Sergeant abroad missing English rum

indicators.note: abroad means the letters are scattered far from home, rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier overseas who has run out of English rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes E from SERGEANT before 'abroad' rearranges the rest. 'rum' is the old British adjective for odd, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum in old British slang means odd or peculiar, a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: European charged outside America is difficult to catch

indicators.note: outside means the word for charged is wrapped around the country

parts.note: a live wire is electrically charged

explanation.surface: A European accused abroad, beyond American reach, evades arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elusive slips away and is hard to grasp or capture.

clue.text: Atrocity committed on a field of battle?

parts.note: an atrocity is a terrible crime

explanation.surface: A war crime carried out on a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean peninsula was the scene of the 1850s Crimean War, so it is one example of a battleground.

clue.text: Itinerant magician's prop turned King Edward into Queen Elizabeth!

parts.note: a wand is the stick a conjuror waves
ER stands for Edwardus Rex, King Edward
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A conjuror's stick transforms one monarch into another.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke: both monarchs share the cipher ER, so the 'transformation' changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer roams from place to place, so is itinerant; the noun stands as one who travels.

clue.text: Drink, one way and another, leads to disturbance

parts.note: rum is a drink

indicators.note: one way and another means a drink read forwards, then a drink read the other way

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Boozing in all sorts of ways ends up in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' does double duty: RUM one way, SUP read the other way as PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumpus is a noisy commotion or uproar.

clue.text: See 4
Craftsman means to groom his boy

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: a man's boy is his son

explanation.surface: A tradesman intends to train up his son.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a skilled worker who cuts and dresses stone.

clue.text: Ass featured in ancient witchcraft

indicators.note: featured in means the letters appear inside the following words

explanation.surface: A donkey appearing in old sorcery tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Ass and twit both mean a fool or silly person.

clue.text: River bird may be a record holder

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a jay is a bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A river bird might be a champion of some sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record holder' suggests a champion, but means one who handles records.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc jockey literally holds the records they play, a playful reading of champion.

clue.text: Soldiers leaving train for another kind of transport

indicators.note: leaving means the soldiers depart from the word for train

parts.note: to rehearse is to train or practise
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops get off a train and take some other vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a railway but is the verb to practise.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the vehicle that carries a coffin, a rather final form of conveyance.
